newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London-based Arab newspapers - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London-based Arab newspapers - May 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in two London-based Arabic-language newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian president urges Europe to play more active role in the Middle East peace process.
- Iran's presidential candidate Nateq-Nouri says Iran's priority is to expel U.S. forces from the Gulf.
- Iraq welcomes Jordan's suggestion to raise trade exchanges between them by $50 million.
- Gulf Arab states face a $14 billion trade deficit with the European Union, GCC secretary general says.
- Syria might cooperate with Iraq if Israel refuses to negotiate on a land-for-peace basis.
- Jordan's Arab Bank announces the setting up of a new Islamic bank with a capital of $56.4 million.
- Jordanian central bank issues certificates of deposit worth $42.3 million.
- Saudi's Makkah for Construction to start next week its second auction to sell 92 flats.
